messages:

Subject: Dedicated capacity: follow-up & targeted sizing questions

Kelsey / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few targeted asks to help Ben and our infra team size a reserved pool that fits Shoply’s profile. I pasted a short worksheet (attached) — would appreciate you filling the highlighted cells where possible.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary workload: customer chat + transactional summarization for checkout flows; occasional batch embedding jobs for search re-index (~nightly).
- SLO: 95th latency target ~120–150ms per request for user-facing chat (50–150 token responses typical).
- Expected initial QPS: 8 sustained, 40 peak; burst events during promos up to ~120 QPS for several minutes.
- Token mix: average prompt 120 tokens, output 80 tokens; ~60% short prompts, 10% >1k token context (rare).
- Security: need VPC peering and SOC2 evidence; data residency in US.

Questions we need from you to finalize SKU options (fill in the workbook if easier):
1) Which model family do you expect to use in production? (open Llama / 7B–13B, 70B, or a commercial LLM)
2) For the chat flows, what percent of requests require full 1k+ context vs short context? You mentioned "rare" — can you quantify (e.g., 5–15%)?
3) Peak burst duration: are promo spikes usually minutes, hours, or days?
4) Any hard latency SLAs tied to business metrics (e.g., conversion drop if >250ms)?
5) Do you plan to run concurrent fine-tuning or large-batch embedding jobs during business hours?

Next steps
- If you can return the workbook by Tue 23 Jun, Ben will propose an A100 vs H100 sku mix and a concurrency plan (continuous batching + pre-warmed slots) for a 90-day reserved pool pilot.
- We’ll include a pricing scenario and a checklist for the VPC/private deployment items.

Attachments: shoply_capacity_workbook_v2.xlsx (worksheet cells highlighted), sample SKU recommendation template.

Thanks — I’ve looped in Laura for procurement questions and Ben for the sizing.

—

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: follow-up & targeted sizing questions

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the clear checklist. Answers inline below and I saved a filled copy of the workbook in the Drive link (shared).

1) Model family: we plan to start on an open 13B for the first quarter and evaluate moving to a 70B for higher quality flows in Q3.
2) Long context: ~8–10% of chat requests use >1k context, most are support tickets where users paste conversation history.
3) Burst duration: promo spikes are typically 10–20 minutes, though we had one incident that ran ~2 hours during a sellout flash. Plan on designing around 15 minute spikes by default.
4) Latency SLA: not a formal SLA, but conversion drop observed after ~300ms. Targeting 120–150ms as you noted keeps a safe margin.
5) Fine-tuning / batch jobs: embeddings are scheduled overnight; we do not run heavy model training during business hours. We may run occasional incremental fine-tunes in the evening window (~9pm–1am PT).

I also added traffic distribution by hour in the workbook and listed our busiest PST window (noon–2pm PST).

Tom and I are aligned to move quickly on a pilot if the reserved pool gives predictable cost and predictable latency. We’ll need SOC2 docs and a checklist for VPC peering — happy to sign an NDA if that helps speed reviews.

Kelsey
Head of Product
Shoply

Jonas — thanks, good signals from Shoply. Quick recommendation below (attaching a short SKU note).

Summary recommendation (pilot — 90d reserved pool)
- Start with a mixed pool: 3 x A100 80GB equiv (or 4 x A100 40GB) for steady baseline; 2 x H100 80GB instances as pre-warmed burst capacity. The H100s give headroom for 70B benching in Q3.
- Concurrency plan: 12 reserved concurrent slots for user-facing chat (continuous batching), with an elastic warm pool of +24 burst slots for promo windows. The continuous batching window should be tuned to 8–12ms to preserve latency.
- Token optimisation: enable prefix KV caching for the 60% short prompts and aggressive caching for vendor IDs and product snippets — expect ~20–30% token-cost reduction for chat flows.
- Model fallbacks: provision a quantized 13B variant for sub-100ms cheap path and the full 70B on H100s for higher-quality calls routed at lower QPS.

Operational asks for Shoply to confirm
- Typical KV cache footprint estimate (MBs per session) — affects memory reservation per slot.
- Nightly batch embedding window (start/end times) so we can schedule GPU affinity.
- VPC peering CIDR and preferred peering window for the pilot.

Attachments: redwood_sku_recommendation.pdf (two SKU scenarios, cost delta table). I based the numbers on the workbook you uploaded. Happy to walk through the calc with pricing.
